questions.q: Why does Driftwood export a `.bacpac` file instead of relying only on Azure SQL's built-in point-in-time restore?
options: Point-in-time restore doesn't actually work
A portable, cloud-agnostic backup file can live outside Azure, which point-in-time restore alone cannot provide
`.bacpac` files are required by AWS
It's faster than point-in-time restore
questions.explain: Point-in-time restore only protects data inside Azure; a portable export is what actually lets a copy live in a second cloud.

questions.q: What triggers the cross-cloud replication workflow?
options: Every push to the `main` branch
A cron schedule, running once every night, independent of any code push
A manual button click in the Azure portal
It only runs once, during initial setup
questions.explain: The workflow uses `on: schedule: cron: "0 7 * * *"` — it's a recurring nightly job, not tied to deploys.

questions.q: How does the workflow get AWS credentials to upload to S3?
options: A static AWS access key and secret key stored in GitHub Secrets
`aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials` exchanges GitHub's OIDC token for short-lived credentials scoped to `driftwood-replication-role`
It uses the same Azure credentials to talk to AWS
It doesn't need AWS credentials because the bucket is public
questions.explain: OIDC token exchange on the AWS side means no static AWS keys are ever stored in GitHub Secrets.

questions.q: What IAM role does this replication job assume, and what can that role actually do?
options: A root-account role with full administrative access
`driftwood-replication-role`, limited to `s3:PutObject` and `s3:ListBucket` on only the backups bucket, per Lesson 6's policy
No specific role; it uses the default AWS account permissions
A role that can also modify the AKS cluster
questions.explain: The role assumed here is exactly the narrowly-scoped one whose IAM policy was written in Lesson 6.

questions.q: What command confirms a backup actually landed in the S3 bucket after a scheduled run?
options: `terraform apply`
`aws s3 ls s3://driftwood-app-backups/`
`kubectl get pods`
`docker build`
questions.explain: Listing the bucket and seeing a new dated prefix confirms the export-to-replication chain worked end to end.
